BURSEVI:v10p283/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p283/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p283/r1.claim: Inwardly, the limited self shortchanges the spirit in true, essential monotheism because it lacks capacity; that tawhid has no counterpart and should not be weighed, while formal monotheism is the self’s due from the spirit.
BURSEVI:v10p283/r1.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى حال النفس القاصرة في التوحيد الحققي فإنها إذا أعطته الروح

BURSEVI:v10p283/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p283/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p283/r2.claim: ‘Do they not think?’ is an interrogative hamza with negation, not an alerting particle, since removing the latter would leave the meaning intact; it may also urge them to think.
BURSEVI:v10p283/r2.anchor: بل الهمزة الاستفهامية الإنكارية داخلة على لا النافية وجوز أن تكون للعرض والتحضيض على الظن

BURSEVI:v10p283/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p283/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p283/r3.claim: The Day is immense and people will be reckoned for even a speck or mustard seed; mention of mere supposition intensifies the warning, since even weak belief would deter cheating, while believers need certainty.
BURSEVI:v10p283/r3.anchor: ومحاسبون فيه على مقدار الذرة والخردلة فإن من يظن ذلك وإن كان ظنا ضعيفا في حد الشك

QASHANI:83:1-5/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:83:1-5/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:83:1-5/r4.claim: They do not expect resurrection and judgment, when inner virtues and vices become visible and cannot be feigned or hidden, bringing shame and consequence.
QASHANI:83:1-5/r4.anchor: الموصوفون بهذه الرذيلة التي هي أفحش أنواع الظلم

SULAMI:v2p380#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p380#2/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p380#2/r1.claim: Those addressed must face reckoning and return to God with their deeds.
SULAMI:v2p380#2/r1.anchor: إنهم لا بد لهم من المحاسبة والرجوع إلى بأعمالهم

SULAMI:v2p380#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p380#2/r2.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v2p380#2/r2.claim: Someone who knows he will be raised and judged yet persists in sins acts as though he does not believe in resurrection and reckoning.
SULAMI:v2p380#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو حفص : من علم انه مبعوث ، وكاسب ثم لا يجتنب المعاصي ، والذنوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r5.claim: The astonished question about resurrection supports taking the initial warning to address Muslims; sincere Muslims stopped cheating, whereas hypocrites did not.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r6.claim: Ẓann means its usual sense: a preponderant belief that the event will occur, as in 45:32.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r6.anchor: والظن : مستعمل في معناه الحقيقي المشهور وهو اعتقاد وقوع الشيء اعتقادا راجحا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r7.claim: The demonstrative “those” singles the cheaters out for public blame and makes their described trait a reason for the rebuke.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p192/r7.anchor: لقصد تمييزهم وتشهير ذكرهم في مقام الذم

NAHHAS:v5p173/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p173/r15.claim: The إن clause and what it governs occupy the two object positions of يظن.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r15.anchor: أن وما عملت فيه في موضع المفعولين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r13.claim: The passage turns to resurrection as a rebuke; this supports a Medinan setting involving believers while applying to the rest of the community too.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r13.anchor: ثم وقفهم تعالى على أمر القيامة وذكرهم بها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r14.claim: Here يظن means to know and be certain.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p53/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p53/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p53/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj reasons that if the defrauders believed they would be resurrected, they would not reduce measures and weights.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p53/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى لو ظنوا أنهم يبعثون ما نقصوا في الكيل والوزن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r13.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r13.claim: Another view takes yadhunnu to mean certainty; al-Zamakhshari prefers the interpretation he gave earlier.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r13.anchor: وقيل : الظن بمعنى اليقين ، والوجه ما ذكر

MUQATIL:83:1-5/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r6.claim: He warns that those who cheat in measure should consider whether they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day.
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r6.anchor: ثم خوفهم فقال: { ألا يظن أولئك } الذين يفعلون هذا { أنهم مبعوثون ليوم عظيم } [آية: 5]

QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r1.claim: The question rebukes traders for acting as if resurrection and accountability never occur; here zann means certainty.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ألا يظن أولئك } إنكار وتعجيب عظيم من حالهم

QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r2.claim: If they truly knew they would be resurrected, they would not reduce measure and weight.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r2.anchor: والظن هنا بمعنى اليقين أي ألا يوقن أولئك، ولو أيقنوا ما نقصوا

QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r3.claim: Alternatively, if they doubt resurrection, they should at least consider it and investigate cautiously.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r3.anchor: وقيل: الظن بمعنى التردد، أي إن كانوا لا يستيقنون بالبعث

QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r7.claim: An Arab rebuked ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan for taking Muslim property without measure, applying the threat to rulers too.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r7.anchor: قد سمعت ما قال الله تعالى في المطففين أراد بذلك أن المطففين قد توجه عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r8.claim: The rebuke, word “think,” great-day description, and people's submission show the gravity of fraud and injustice in all dealings and acts.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:4-6/r8.anchor: وفي هذا الإنكار والتعجيب وكلمة الظن، ووصف اليوم بالعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r1.claim: One reading takes ẓann as knowledge; the addressees may be believing Aws and Khazraj, whom the Prophet reminded of their already-held belief in resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r1.anchor: أن المراد منه العلم ، وعلى هذا التقدير يحتمل أن يكون المخاطبون بهذا الخطاب من جملة المصدقين بالبعث

RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r2.claim: On the same reading, even people who deny resurrection can be urged to infer it rationally from the need, or at least possibility, of recompense for good and evil.
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r2.anchor: كانوا متمكنين من الاستدلال عليه ، لما في العقول من إيصال الجزاء إلى المحسن والمسيء

RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r3.claim: Inferential knowledge can be called “supposition” because it rests on what is most probable, unlike doubt where both alternatives are equal.
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r3.anchor: لأن أكثر العلوم الاستدلالية راجع إلى الأغلب في الرأي ، ولم يكن كالشك الذي يعتدل الوجهان فيه

RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r4.claim: A second reading takes ẓann literally: even without certainty, people should at least suspect a resurrection, since God's wisdom and mercy would not neglect them after death; that suspicion should suffice to make them fear.
RAZI-FULL:v31p82#2/r4.anchor: القول الثاني : أن المراد من الظن ههنا هو الظن نفسه لا العلم

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r1.claim: The soundest meaning of people standing for their Lord is standing for judgment, where trivial fraud is shown to have accumulated into a great wrong.
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r1.anchor: وهو الأصح أن الناس يقومون لمحاسبة رب العالمين

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God restores souls to bodies, and those bodies rise from their graves.
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r2.anchor: أنه سبحانه يرد الأرواح إلى أجسادها فتقوم تلك الأجساد من مراقدها

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r3.claim: Abū Muslim understands the standing as people standing in worship and obedience solely for God, like “stand for God devoutly.”
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r3.anchor: قال أبو مسلم معنى : { يقوم الناس } هو كقوله : { وقوموا لله قانتين }

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r4.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r4.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar quoting the Prophet says each person stands submerged in sweat up to half his ears.
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r4.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله : { يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين } قال : ( يقوم أحدكم

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar wept so intensely while reciting this verse that he could not continue.
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عمر : أنه قرأ هذه السورة ، فلما بلغ قوله { يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين } بكى نحيبا

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r6.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says the people stand for three hundred worldly years without being given any order.
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r6.anchor: روى عنه عليه السلام أنه قال : ( يقوم الناس مقدار ثلثمائة سنة من الدنيا لا يؤمر فيهم بأمر )

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says they remain for forty years and are then addressed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r7.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود : ( يمكثون أربعين عاما ثم يخاطبون )

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the standing lasts for believers only about as long as it takes them to finish a prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : وهو في حق المؤمنين كقدر انصرافهم من الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r10.claim: Though the fraud is tiny, universal judgment displays God's wisdom: vindicating the wronged over even a small amount shows the precision of divine knowledge and justice.
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r10.anchor: عظمة الحكمة لا تظهر إلا بأن انتصف للمظلوم من الظالم بسبب ذلك القدر الحقير الطفيف

STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r1.claim: The sūrah may be late Makkan, early Madinan, or a combination of both.
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r1.anchor: is a late Makkan or early Madinan sūrah, or a combination of the two.

STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r2.speaker: Bg, IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r2.claim: One account places the first four verses just after the Prophet arrived in Madinah, verses 5–28 in Madinah, and the final eight among the last verses revealed in Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r2.anchor: The first four verses were reportedly revealed just after the Prophet’s arrival in Madinah

SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r1.claim: The apparent reading is ألا as an exhortative particle urging them to consider, with ظن meaning certainty.
SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنها " ألا " التحضيضية، حضهم على ذلك، ويكون الظن بمعنى اليقين

SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r2.claim: An alternative parses ألا as a negation particle preceded by the interrogative hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:83:4/r2.anchor: وقيل: هل لا النافية دخلت عليها همزة الاستفهام

ZAJJAJ:v5p298/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p298/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p298/r1.claim: The great day is the Resurrection; if the defrauders believed they would be resurrected, they would not cheat in measure or weight.
ZAJJAJ:v5p298/r1.anchor: يعنى يوم القيامة، أي إنهم لو ظنوا أنهم يبعثون ما نقصوا في الكيل

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r9.claim: The question rebukes and expresses astonishment; the far demonstrative distances the cheaters from God's mercy, and the Great Day is the Resurrection when they are repaid.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r9.anchor: الاستفهام للإنكار والتعجيب، والظن بمعناه المعروف والإشارة إلى المطففين بأولئك الموضوعة للاشارة البعيدة للدلالة على بعدهم من رحمة الله،

TABRISI:83:1-3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:83:1-3/r11.claim: “The day people stand” is accusative, governed by “raised,” meaning the day they are resurrected.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r11.anchor: يوم يقوم الناس منصوب بقوله مبعوثون أي ألا يظنون

THALABI:v10p151/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p151/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p151/r5.claim: The question means that cheaters should know with certainty they will be raised for a tremendous day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds.
THALABI:v10p151/r5.anchor: ألا يظن يستيقن أولئك أنهم مبعوثون ليوم عظيم يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين

THALABI:v10p151/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p151/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v10p151/r6.claim: A listener reports Ibn Umar weeping and falling when he recited the Day people stand before God, unable to continue.
THALABI:v10p151/r6.anchor: فلما بلغ يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين بكى حتى خروا وامتنع من قراءة ما بعده

ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.claim: Authentic traditions cited by Tabari, Baghawi, and Ibn Kathir place at least the first four verses shortly after the Prophet's arrival in Medina.
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.anchor: However, a number of authentic Traditions make it clear that at least the first four verses were

ASAD-NOTES:83:4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:4/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:4/r1.claim: The wrongdoers are to be raised and called to account on the awesome Day when everyone stands before the Sustainer of all worlds.
ASAD-NOTES:83:4/r1.anchor: on an awesome Day (83:6) the Day when all men shall stand

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r11.claim: Cheaters would not dare such fraud if they firmly believed, or even considered it possible, that they would be resurrected.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r11.anchor: bunu muhtemel görmeleri halinde bile bu sahtekârlığa cüret etmelerinin mümkün olmadığına dikkat çekilmektedir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.claim: Sūrah al-Muṭaffifīn supplements al-Infiṭār, sharing its theme and elaborating the division of righteous and defiant people at its end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.anchor: This sūrah  is a supplement to S ūrah al-Infi ṭār

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.claim: Al-Infiṭār reasons from God’s attributes displayed in the human body, while this sūrah reasons from the moral nature God gave people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.anchor: attributes of God that are prominent in man’s physical being

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r5.claim: Since God is just and created people with a love of justice, He must establish a day to reward those who honor that nature and punish those who disregard it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r5.anchor: it is essential that He bring forth a day in which He

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly uses this reasoning for the Day of Judgement; the author points to his discussion of 75:14–15.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.anchor: readers can take a look at what I have written under the following verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.claim: Verses 1–6 censure people who demand fair treatment while cheating others; their conduct shows they do not expect to be raised before their Lord for judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.anchor: An expression of regret on people who want

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.claim: This nature shows that people distinguish good from evil and expect different treatment; God must therefore judge righteous and wrongdoers, and the deniers resist because they wish to evade that outcome.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.anchor: An obvious corollary of this is that the Almighty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r2.claim: The question expresses wonder at disbelievers’ attitude: everyone should fear the great day attested by human nature, when people rise before the Creator and are judged and recompensed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r2.anchor: These verses express wonder at the attitude adopted

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r3.claim: The phrase Lord of the worlds carries arguments for the majesty and necessity of the Day and its judgements, which the author has explained elsewhere.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r3.anchor: the majesty and need of such a day and the verdicts given therein

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r1.claim: The question admonishes them to recognize resurrection; it can mean being raised on a great day or being raised for that day's reckoning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r1.anchor: ألا يظن: توقيف على أمر القيامة وإنكار عليهم في فعلهم ذلك، أي ليوم عظيم، وهو يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r3.claim: He takes يوم as a substitute for يوم عظيم; one transmitted reading puts it in genitive after ليوم, while Zayd ibn Ali reads it nominative, ‘that is a day.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو بدل من يوم عظيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r4.claim: يظن can mean to know with certainty, or retain its ordinary sense of weighing or expecting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r4.anchor: ويظن بمعنى يوقن، أو هو على وضعه من الترجيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r5.claim: The rebuke, the day's greatness, people's humbled standing before the Lord of all worlds, and the wording about His lordship all show the enormity of cheating.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r5.anchor: وفي هذا الإنكار والتعجب، ووصف اليوم بالعظم، وقيام الناس لله خاضعين، ووصفه برب العالمين، دليل على عظم هذا الذنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r7.claim: كلا rebukes the cheats for their conduct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p427/r7.anchor:
كلا:
ردع لما كانوا عليه من التطفيف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r1.claim: The renewed question magnifies the enormity of their fraud: the initial hamza conveys denial and astonishment, joined to a negative la, rather than an introductory or attention-getting particle; “belief” retains its ordinary sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r1.anchor: استئناف وارد لتهويل ماما ارتكبوه من التطفيف والهمزة لإنكار والتعجيب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r2.claim: “Those” points to the defrauders, highlighting their defining vice and setting them apart; its distance suggests how far they are from goodness and corruption, so the question denies they believe in resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p70/r2.anchor: ووضعه موضع ضميرهم للإشعار بمناط الحكم الذي هو وصفهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362#2/r1.claim: Ala yaẓunnu means do they not know with certainty that the fraudulent will be resurrected for the great Day, the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362#2/r1.anchor: {ألا يظن} يستيقن {أولئك} الذين يفعلون ذلك {أنهم مبعوثون ليوم عظيم} يعني يوم القيامة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r3.claim: Anyone who believed in resurrection would not dare such offenses; the verse rebukes their behavior, even more so if they were certain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r3.anchor: فإن من ظن ذلك لم يتجاسر على أمثال هذه القبائح، فكيف بمن تيقنه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the warning to the record of every deed in 82:10 and the exact weighing of deeds in 21:47; fraud may seem small but is a major crime and merits a great warning.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r2.claim: Their habitual vice follows from feeling safe from punishment and denying the final accounting; the rhetorical question suggests even a mere suspicion of resurrection should restrain them, since decisive proofs have been given.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r2.anchor: وكان ذلك لا يكون إلا ممن أمن العقاب وأنكر الحساب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r3.claim: Resurrection is a compelled awakening like rising from sleep, for the great day of gathering and accounting, when reward and punishment follow deeds; only God knows its full reality.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r3.anchor: بالبعث الذي قد ألفوا مثله من القهر باليقظة بعد القهر بالنوم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r1.claim: Some interpret lā in lā uqsim as negating the oath itself; the author rejects this in favor of denying the need to swear.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r1.anchor: وفرقً بعيد أقصى البعد، بين أن تكون "لا" لنفي القسم، كما قال بعضهم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r2.claim: The Quranic formula denies God's need to swear, making the context itself attest to certainty and thereby affirming and establishing the message.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r2.anchor: ومن نفي الحاجة إلى القسم، يأتي التوثيق والتقرير. لأنه يجعل المقام في غنى بالثقة واليقين عن الإقسام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r3.claim: Ordinary Arabic similarly confirms trust by saying 'do not swear' or 'I need no oath,' just as 'I need not urge you' strengthens an instruction.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r3.anchor: فتقول لمن تثق فيه: لا تقسم، أو: من غير يمين. مقررأ بذلك أنه موضع ثقتك

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r4.claim: She says this study does not deny the early generations' service; their generous contribution has remained a store and support for later generations.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p285/r4.anchor: ألا يُظن بي أنني أجحد جهود السلف الصالح في خدمة كتاب الإسلام

BURHAN:v3p344/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p344/r7.speaker: أبو الفتح
BURHAN:v3p344/r7.claim: Abu al-Fath allows ظن to mean either certainty or its usual sense here; the latter is stronger, since even imagining the great resurrection should deter sin, all the more so certainty.

BURHAN:v3p344/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p344/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p344/r8.claim: The author prefers the ordinary sense of ظن: mere awareness of the resurrection's enormity should restrain wrongdoing, so certain knowledge would do so more powerfully.
BURHAN:v3p344/r8.anchor: وهو أقوى في المعنى أي فقد يمنع من هذا التوهم فكيف عند تحقيق الأمر فهذا أبلغ كقوله يكفيك من شر سماعه

BURHAN:v4p155/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r1.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p155/r1.claim: Ibn Malik says ظن is restricted to certainty.
BURHAN:v4p155/r1.anchor: وذكر ابن مالك انها تختص باليقين

BURHAN:v4p155/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r2.speaker: غيره
BURHAN:v4p155/r2.claim: Other scholars say ظن can also mean doubt, citing the command to accept the women as believers if they are known to be so.
BURHAN:v4p155/r2.anchor: وذكر غيره انها تستعمل في الظن ايضا بدليل قوله ﴿ فإن علمتموهن مؤمنات ﴾ 5

BURHAN:v4p155/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p155/r3.claim: Zarkashi's proposed reply is that علم retains its literal sense here and ايمان means verbal affirmation, so the cited verse need not show that ظن means doubt.
BURHAN:v4p155/r3.anchor: وله أن يقول العلم على حقيقيته والمراد بالايمان التصديق اللساني

BURHAN:v4p155/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p155/r4.claim: ظن can mean certainty because it contains an element of certainty; without that element it would be ignorance. Zarkashi cites several Qur'anic examples, including this verse.
BURHAN:v4p155/r4.anchor: وقد تستعمل بمعنى اليقين لان الظن فيه طرف من اليقين لولاه كان جهلا

BURHAN:v4p155/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p155/r5.claim: Zarkashi gives a contextual test: praiseworthy, rewarded ظن means certainty; blameworthy, threatened ظن means doubt.
BURHAN:v4p155/r5.anchor: حيث وجد الظن محمودا مثابا عليه فهو اليقين وحيث وجد مذموما متوعدا بالعقاب عليه فهو الشك

BURHAN:v4p155/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p155/r6.claim: A ظن followed by light إن indicates doubt; examples include a couple's fear of failing to keep God's limits and the assumption that the Messenger would not return.
BURHAN:v4p155/r6.anchor: أن كل ظن يتصل بعده إن الخفيفة فهو شك كقوله ﴿ إن ظنا أن يقيما حدود الله ﴾ 1

BURHAN:v4p155/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p155/r7.claim: A ظن followed by emphatic إن indicates certainty; Zarkashi cites the present verse and two other passages.
BURHAN:v4p155/r7.anchor: وكل ظن يتصل به إن المشددة فالمراد به اليقين كقوله ﴿ إني ظننت أني ملاق حسابيه ﴾ 7

BURHAN:v4p155/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p155/r8.claim: The emphatic إن marks certainty, while the light form signals its opposite; examples contrast علم أن with حسبوا ألا, where حسبان means doubt.
BURHAN:v4p155/r8.anchor: والمعنى فيه إن المشددة للتأكيد فدخلت على اليقين وإن الخفيفة بخلافها فدخلت في الشك

BURHAN:v4p155/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p155/r9.claim: Zarkashi addresses ظنوا أن لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه as an apparent counterexample, explaining that إن is attached to the verb.
BURHAN:v4p155/r9.anchor: فإن قيل يرد على هذا الضابط قوله تعالى ﴿ وظنوا أن لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه ﴾ 12 قيل لانها اتصلت بالفعل

BURHAN:v4p155/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r10.speaker: الراغب
BURHAN:v4p155/r10.claim: Al-Raghib defines ظن as a broad term spanning doubt and certainty: it is based on an indicator, reaching knowledge when strong and mere supposition when very weak.
BURHAN:v4p155/r10.anchor: ثم رأيت الراغب قال في تفسير سورة البقرة الظن أعم ألفاظ الشك واليقين وهو اسم لما حصل عن أمارة

BURHAN:v4p155/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p155/r11.speaker: الراغب
BURHAN:v4p155/r11.claim: Al-Raghib says stronger ظن takes emphatic or light أن, whereas weak ظن takes إن with an imperfect; the first sense is praiseworthy and the second blameworthy.
BURHAN:v4p155/r11.anchor: فمتى قويت أدت إلى العلم ومتى ضعفت جدا لم تتجاوز حد الوهم
